app.name: Application Programs
app.detail: compiler, assembler, text editor, database, games, business programs

os.name: Operating System
os.detail: interface between the user and the hardware

hw.name: Hardware
hw.detail: CPU, memory, I/O devices, system bus

steps.press: User 1 presses Ctrl+S in a text editor
steps.request: the text editor asks the OS to save the file
steps.command: the OS tells the hardware (disk) to write the data
steps.reply: the OS tells the text editor it worked
steps.see: User 1 sees the file has been saved

user.name: User
user.reason: to them, a computer is just a bunch of applications

programmer.name: Programmer
programmer.reason: needs utilities to build applications with machine-language instructions

designer.name: OS designer
designer.reason: has to know how the hardware works

osDefinitions.title: Seven Definitions of an OS
osDefinitions.closing: There's no single best definition. It's easier to define an OS by <mark>what it does</mark> than by what it is.

hardwareController.name: Hardware controller
hardwareController.definition: software that controls the hardware, just an ordinary program (like some files in DOS)

abstraction.name: Abstraction
abstraction.definition: a program that makes the hardware easier to use

workOrganizer.name: Work organizer
workOrganizer.definition: a set of programs that manages how the hardware works, e.g. serving user requests

resourceManager.name: Resource manager
resourceManager.definition: a resource manager/allocator, e.g. managing memory, printers, etc.

controlProgram.name: Control program
controlProgram.definition: a program used to control other programs

kernel.name: Kernel
kernel.definition: a program that keeps running the whole time the computer is on

guardian.name: Guardian
guardian.definition: keeps the computer safe from all kinds of computer crime
